_sources.usda: USDA FoodData Central, https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/ (record named in each entry), read 2026-10-27
_sources.nihOds: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements fact sheets (Iron, Folate, Vitamin C, Vitamin K, Magnesium, Zinc, Potassium, Vitamin A, Calcium, Vitamin B12, Vitamin D, Vitamin E), https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/list-all/; reference intakes as listed in build_draft_batch.py (RDA for adult women)
_sources.niddk: NIDDK, Eating, Diet & Nutrition for Kidney Stones, read 2026-10-26: nuts and nut products, peanuts, rhubarb, spinach and wheat bran listed among foods to reduce for calcium oxalate stones

concord-grape.how: Eat fresh as a snack (the skins slip off, and the seeds are edible), or chill them first for a cold snack.
concord-grape.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
concord-grape.reviewNote: USDA's American-type slip-skin grape is the Concord type. Grape juice is a different food.
concord-grape.name: Concord grape

lemon.how: Squeeze juice over fish, vegetables and salads, or add zest to baking and dressings.
lemon.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
lemon.reviewNote: Whole lemon without peel; most people use juice or a wedge, so the serving here is much larger than a squeeze.
lemon.name: Lemon

lime.how: Squeeze over tacos, soups, salads and drinks, or use the zest in marinades.
lime.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
lime.reviewNote: A whole lime is a larger serving than the juice or wedge people usually use.
lime.name: Lime

sour-cherry.how: Cook into compotes, pies and sauces with some sweetener, since they are tart; or eat them fresh if you like the tartness.
sour-cherry.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
sour-cherry.reviewNote: Raw sour cherries; tart cherry juice and dried cherries are separate foods.
sour-cherry.name: Sour cherry

lychee.how: Peel, remove the seed and eat fresh, or add to fruit salad.
lychee.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
lychee.name: Lychee

coconut.how: Eat fresh pieces as a snack, or grate or shave over porridge, yoghurt and curries.
coconut.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
coconut.reviewNote: Raw coconut meat. Coconut milk, coconut water and coconut oil are separate foods with different composition. This is a high-fat food (about 34 g per 100 g, mostly saturated); no amount is recommended here.
coconut.name: Coconut

guava.how: Eat ripe fruit fresh, skin and all, or slice into fruit salad.
guava.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
guava.name: Guava

persimmon.how: Eat a ripe Fuyu type like an apple, or scoop soft ripe Hachiya type with a spoon.
persimmon.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
persimmon.reviewNote: Japanese persimmon, the common supermarket type. USDA's "native" (American) persimmon record is a different fruit with sparse data and was not used. Dried persimmon is far more concentrated.
persimmon.name: Persimmon

date.how: Eat on their own, stuffed with nut butter, or chop into porridge and baking.
date.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
date.reviewNote: Medjool dates; the existing catalogue entry does not say which variety, and deglet noor dates differ somewhat. Dates are concentrated in sugar (about 66 g per 100 g by the record's carbohydrate).
date.name: Date

raisin.desc: Raisins, dark, seedless (Includes foods for USDA's Food Distribution Program)
raisin.how: Add to porridge, salads and baking, or eat a small handful as a snack.
raisin.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
raisin.reviewNote: Dark seedless raisins; golden raisins (often treated with sulphites) are a separate USDA record.
raisin.name: Raisin

cranberry.how: Cook with a sweetener into sauces and compotes, or add to baking; raw cranberries are very tart.
cranberry.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
cranberry.reviewNote: Raw cranberries (tart). Dried sweetened cranberries and cranberry juice are different foods.
cranberry.name: Cranberry

dried-apricots.how: Eat a few as a snack, chop into porridge and grain dishes, or simmer into compotes.
dried-apricots.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
dried-apricots.reviewNote: Sulfured dried apricots (the orange kind); unsulfured ones are brown and the record differs. Sulphite sensitivity is a real caution for sulphited dried fruit; the catalogue caution is carried over without an external source here.
dried-apricots.name: Dried apricots

prunes.how: Eat a few as a snack, stew them, or chop into baking and porridge.
prunes.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
prunes.name: Prunes (dried plums)
